constraints: The active context needs bounded relevant results.
The full result set must remain queryable through explicit continuation and detail paths.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The design may require another tool call for a broad question, but it protects attention and makes completeness an observable choice.
details.errorCorrection: Put result shaping at the tool boundary and make truncation or continuation explicit; do not rely on the model to recover from an oversized or silently incomplete response.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Programmatic filtering and pagination process results before model exposure; a continuation token and record-ID lookup provide deliberate expansion when the user needs it.
details.scenarioApplication: Filter by claim and active policy version, return a small ranked page, and let Claude request the next page or exact clause instead of receiving 10,000 rows.
details.transfer: For large intermediate results, process and bound them before model context while preserving an explicit path to inspect the authoritative source.

messages.text: Pagination alone still returns broad pages and leaves selection to the model; without claim-specific filters and a record-level detail contract, the relevant clause can remain buried and page requests become model-driven.
Silent truncation can hide the relevant clause and gives no reliable way to tell whether the first page was complete.
A count alone removes the evidence needed for the answer and turns an addressable tool problem into unnecessary manual work.

feedback.reason: The tool should constrain intermediate context without hiding valid evidence. Pagination and detail lookup preserve access to the full set while making the common claim query focused.

options.text: Return the complete result set in pages but place the first page in context and ask Claude to summarize before requesting more pages.
Return a fixed first page of ten rows and rely on the model to continue only when it recognizes that the target claim is absent.
Return a filtered count plus a human-operated search link, leaving the assistant unable to retrieve an exact clause during the normal path.
Require filters and pagination, return concise matches with a continuation token, and expose a bounded detail lookup by record ID.

prompt: A claims assistant receives every matching policy record, sometimes 10,000 rows, even when the user asks about one claim. The model then misses the relevant clause. Which tool boundary should replace that response shape?

constraints: Each exposed capability should have one distinct operation and a predictable filter contract.
The selection errors occur among overlapping tools rather than from a missing finance data source.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Consolidation may require callers to migrate and can remove convenient aliases, but it lowers wrong-tool calls and protects the typed authorization boundary.
details.errorCorrection: Diagnose overlapping capability surfaces before adding prompt prose, retries, or unrestricted database access.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Distinct tool schemas and descriptions give each operation a clear selection boundary; typed validation rejects unsupported filters before execution.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep one exact invoice lookup and one filtered search, document their identifier and filter semantics, and evaluate selection and parameter validity on representative requests.
details.transfer: When similar tools cause selection errors, reduce the canonical surface and test operation and parameter contracts instead of increasing choice.

messages.text: More aliases preserve four competing contracts and add wording without removing the ambiguity that caused the wrong selection.
Calling every tool multiplies latency and permissions and still leaves the model to reconcile incompatible filters.
Arbitrary database access bypasses typed and authorized capability boundaries and makes the selection problem less observable.

feedback.reason: The defect is capability ambiguity: overlapping names and incompatible filters make a valid request map to the wrong contract. Canonical tools reduce choices and make parameters testable.

options.text: Add aliases and examples for all four tools so Claude has more wording clues while preserving the overlapping contracts.
Call all four tools for each request, compare their results, and let Claude choose the most complete invoice record.
Consolidate the overlapping surface into canonical identifier and search tools with distinct names, filters, and contract tests.
Expose the underlying database for arbitrary queries so Claude can bypass the ambiguous tool descriptions.

prompt: A finance assistant has four tools named fetch_invoice, search_invoice, lookup_invoice, and retrieve_invoice. They accept different filters, overlap in purpose, and the assistant often selects a contract that cannot satisfy the request. What should be diagnosed first?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A combined payload is reasonable for a workflow that consistently needs all three values and has a small bounded result.
details.errorCorrection: Prompt filtering still transports the oversized payload, deleting data fails other workflows, and the full database broadens scope.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Tool output size is part of capability design; response fields should track the caller’s information need.
details.scenarioApplication: Return the stock fact and offer separate bounded retrieval for orders or forecast.
details.transfer: Curate result shape as well as the list of callable operations.

messages.text: The model still receives the oversized payload before it can ignore fields.
Discarding valid order and forecast data breaks other supported requests.
A full database response is broader and larger than the current-stock question.

feedback.reason: The frequent question needs one current value, while other valid data has distinct use. Explicit bounded follow-up access avoids repeatedly paying for unused fields without deleting them.

options.text: Return stock by default; expose pending orders and forecasts through bounded, explicit follow-ups.
Return only current stock and permanently discard the other data for all workflows.
Return the full warehouse database so the model can select the needed columns.
Keep the combined response and instruct Claude to ignore irrelevant sections.

prompt: A warehouse assistant uses a tool called get_inventory. It returns current stock, pending orders, and a seven-day forecast in one 9,000-token response; users usually ask for current stock only. Which output contract should replace it?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A governed analyst product may need an advanced query surface, but its authorization and query constraints must be explicit and enforced.
details.errorCorrection: A stronger prompt leaves the overbroad interface intact; disabling analytics breaks the use case; schema inspection does not enforce policy.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Capability curation defines the operations available to the agent; instructions alone do not constrain an arbitrary query interface.
details.scenarioApplication: Expose the three supported aggregates with enumerated dimensions and bounded filters.
details.transfer: Constrain tool capability at its executable boundary when the current interface is broader than the task.

messages.text: Instructions do not constrain an SQL interface that can query restricted tables.
Disabling all analytics removes the three valid aggregate workflows along with the risky surface.
Schema visibility helps the model reason but does not restrict executable queries.

feedback.reason: The current capability itself permits access beyond the approved analytics. Typed operations narrow what can be requested at the tool boundary rather than relying on model interpretation.

options.text: Let Claude inspect the schema first and decide which tables are appropriate.
Keep SQL and add a stronger instruction that queries must stay within approved tables.
Disable all analytics and ask analysts to export CSV files manually.
Replace arbitrary SQL with three typed aggregates that enforce approved tables and dimensions server-side.

prompt: An analytics agent can call a query tool that accepts arbitrary SQL. Analysts need only three approved aggregates, and a prompt injection once induced a query over a restricted table. What is the smallest coherent tool redesign?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If complete evidence shows no required consumer and an approved deprecation process exists, a later removal decision may be justified.
details.errorCorrection: Main-catalog-only data misses usage; retaining everything forever ignores evidence; replacement before contract review is speculative.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Capability removal depends on complete inventory and actual workflow ownership, not a single telemetry view.
details.scenarioApplication: Inspect both discovery paths and test the emergency workflow’s required contract.
details.transfer: Validate inventory completeness and dependency ownership before treating low observed frequency as dead capability.

messages.text: The primary report omits an entire discovery path, so its zero-use count is not a complete dependency signal.
Keeping entries without ownership or lifecycle evidence avoids deciding whether an operation is truly obsolete.
Reported frequency does not establish that the general tool preserves the emergency workflow contract.

feedback.reason: The current usage source is incomplete and the rare operations have an explicit contractual use. Removal cannot be justified from a partial call count; first establish complete usage and dependency evidence.

options.text: Retain every tool without an owner, last-used date, or deprecation review to avoid any chance of regression.
Replace the emergency template with an existing general tool based on its low reported use, without verifying contract coverage.
Join both catalogs’ usage and verify the emergency-workflow dependency before proposing deletions.
Remove tools with no calls in the primary catalog report, then defer reviewing alternate discovery-path logs until after cleanup.

prompt: A catalog-cleanup proposal would remove the least-used 10% of tools. Usage logs omit tools available through a separate regional discovery endpoint, and those tools support a contractual emergency workflow. What should the owner do before removal?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A combined endpoint can be safe only if the server exposes an equally explicit, typed, validated state machine; the current contract does not.
details.errorCorrection: A prompt instruction or overloaded action enum is not a transaction boundary.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Capability design should make operations and their input requirements explicit; the server remains responsible for consequential authorization.
details.scenarioApplication: A preview can return the proposed transfer and a short-lived approval handle; execution accepts that handle only after the authorizing service validates it.
details.transfer: Split operations when their side effects, approval prerequisites, or retry behavior differ materially.

messages.text: One field with two side-effect semantics makes it easy to confuse a preview with a transfer and weakens validation.
Prompt text cannot turn an immediate mutation into a preview or enforce approval at the server boundary.
Direct database access does not create a safe preview/execution boundary and exposes a broader capability than required.

feedback.reason: Preview and execution have different side-effect contracts. Model the non-mutating operation separately and require the application to validate authorization at execution.

options.text: Add an optional `preview_or_execute` string and let Claude decide which meaning applies on each call.
Separate a non-mutating preview from execution, which must validate an approval token server-side.
Keep the execute tool unchanged and place “preview first” in the system prompt.
Return the account database to Claude so it can calculate the transfer and ask for approval in its final response.

prompt: A settlement tool takes an amount and account ID. A new workflow asks Claude to first preview a transfer and then execute it only after an approval token is issued. The current tool executes immediately and has no preview or approval field. Which capability change best preserves a clear contract?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the snapshot expires or a page fails, report a partial export and restart or resume only under the service contract.
details.errorCorrection: A maximum-sized first page is still partial when `has_more` is true. Guessing page size or deduplicating mutable pages cannot establish completeness.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A bounded collection API should expose explicit continuation and completeness state; a snapshot token can keep a multi-page read consistent when records change.
details.scenarioApplication: Follow the opaque cursor under the same snapshot until the service signals the final page; only then label the export complete.
details.transfer: Design list operations so callers can distinguish partial pages from a complete collection.

messages.text: The service explicitly indicates that more invoices exist; page size does not make the first response complete.
A model cannot infer the correct next page size, and page length is not a completeness signal.
Descriptions may collide, and separate pages can observe different collection states without the snapshot token.

feedback.reason: A page limit bounds each response, while the cursor and snapshot token preserve continuation and a consistent view. `has_more` means the first response is incomplete.

options.text: Return the first page and label it complete because the service selected the largest supported page size.
Expose bounded pages with the cursor and snapshot token; continue until the terminal page before claiming a complete export.
Ask Claude to request larger pages until the returned record count looks representative.
Fetch each page without a snapshot token and deduplicate by invoice description after collection.

prompt: A billing tool returns the first 500 invoices with `has_more=true` and an opaque cursor. Records may change while a request is paged, and the service can pin all pages to one snapshot token. Analysts require an exact complete export. What contract should the assistant use?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a cursor expires or a page fails, expose a partial result rather than silently upgrading it to complete.
details.errorCorrection: A fixed page limit, sample inference, or locally re-labeled result can produce a false exact count.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Pagination state is part of the operation contract; a nonempty result does not prove the collection is complete.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep `has_more` and the opaque cursor in the typed response, or call a supported authoritative count endpoint.
details.transfer: Teach callers to distinguish a successful page from a complete collection.

messages.text: Page size can improve coverage but the exact total still requires terminal-page or authoritative count evidence.
The model cannot infer unseen records reliably, and a likely count is not an exact total.
The wrapper can preserve continuation, but the requested exact count remains unanswered without completing pagination or using an authoritative count.

feedback.reason: A successful first page is still partial when the service signals more results. The wrapper must preserve completeness and continuation semantics.

options.text: Increase the page size and preserve the service’s `has_more` flag, then report the exact count only after checking whether another cursor remains.
Ask the model to estimate the unseen remainder from the returned rows, and label the result as a likely policy-set total.
Preserve the service completeness flag and cursor; report a total only after the terminal page or an authoritative count.
Return the first page with its cursor and ask users to continue manually when they need a whole-set count.

prompt: A wrapper returns 100 policy rows, sets `complete=true` whenever the array is nonempty, and drops the service’s `has_more` flag. Users ask for an exact count across the whole policy set. Traces show the first page is returned successfully. What is the smallest reliable correction?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If one unified operation is needed, a required discriminator plus branch-specific validation can preserve a single endpoint safely.
details.errorCorrection: Prompt reminders cannot enforce a permissive executor boundary; removing validation hides rather than fixes invalid combinations.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A tool schema should make valid operations and their inputs explicit, with server-side validation preserving the same contract.
details.scenarioApplication: The diff and malformed-field trace point to the union interface, not to a demonstrated model capability regression.
details.transfer: Diagnose the contract that changed before replacing a model.

messages.text: Prompt examples cannot enforce the server-side schema or prevent invalid cross-action fields from being accepted.
The action can remain ambiguous and a preview does not correct the invalid operation contract or model behavior.
The widened schema is the direct contract regression; changing models leaves invalid combinations accepted by the server.

feedback.reason: The artifact diff introduced ambiguous combinations and the traces show invalid cross-action fields. Narrow schemas or a discriminated contract address that path.

options.text: Restore explicit operation-specific schemas or a validated discriminated union, and reject fields that do not belong to the selected action.
Retain the union operation but require the model to name one action first, add examples that omit unrelated fields, and prompt it to validate the selected branch before calling.
Keep permissive parsing but route ambiguous combinations to a read-only preview so the backend can disambiguate safely.
Roll back the model and preserve the union schema until a separate evaluation proves the new model can follow its optional fields.

prompt: A deployment diff replaces four narrow invoice operations with `invoice_action`, a union schema containing 18 optional fields. The server now accepts invalid field combinations, and malformed calls rise from 0.3% to 4.1%; logs show the model often supplies both `invoice_id` and `customer_id` to unrelated actions. Which repair best targets the failure?

constraints: The visible workflow needs two narrow operations.
Invalid filter and output combinations should be unrepresentable or rejected before execution.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Some future modes need a separate tool or contract, but the current workflow gains predictable calls and fewer retry loops.
details.errorCorrection: Simplify the canonical capability boundary around actual operations instead of compensating for a broad schema with more prose or retries.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Typed narrow tools reduce the model-visible action space and allow application validation to reject unsupported combinations before an expensive or failing call.
details.scenarioApplication: Use an ID lookup for exact records and a date-bounded search for ranges, with required identifiers or dates and clear result contracts.
details.transfer: When a tool union creates invalid combinations, split by operation and validate the narrow contract before execution.

messages.text: Examples can guide selection but do not make incompatible optional fields impossible and leave retries as the error control.
Hiding modes while preserving the union still exposes the same parameter ambiguity and makes the schema disagree with the intended capability.
Normalizing after a service error spends a call and treats a preventable contract defect as runtime recovery.

feedback.reason: A union-shaped tool makes the model choose among combinations the workflow does not need. Two purpose-specific schemas make required fields and invalid modes explicit before execution.

options.text: Keep one universal tool with examples for common combinations, validate only after a service error, and let the model retry with a revised optional-field set.
Hide the four output modes in prose while retaining their union schema, then accept the model's selected mode when the backend can coerce it.
Split the surface into typed identifier-lookup and date-bounded-search tools with required fields, and remove unused modes from this workflow.
Accept every parameter combination and normalize incompatible filters in a gateway after the reporting service rejects the request.

prompt: A reporting tool exposes eighteen optional filters, four mutually exclusive output modes, and nullable identifiers. Malformed combinations cause retries, although this workflow needs only ID lookup and date-bounded search. Which redesign is best?

constraints: The aggregate must be complete and arithmetically correct.
Operators still need a bounded path to inspect representative source events.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A separate detail call adds interaction for forensic questions, but it protects aggregate correctness and avoids a massive token and latency cost.
details.errorCorrection: Process large intermediate results before exposing them to Claude; preserve source addresses instead of using context size as an implicit sampling rule.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Programmatic filtering and aggregation handle arithmetic and membership; the model receives a compact result and can request a deliberately bounded detail view.
details.scenarioApplication: Filter by audit scope, group by actor and day, return counts with selected event IDs and time ranges, and fetch details only for requested IDs.
details.transfer: For analytics over large records, keep computation and completeness in the structured service and expose compact, auditable evidence handles.

messages.text: Raw rows pollute context and make completeness and arithmetic depend on the model receiving every event.
A random sample cannot answer a complete count and offers no path to verify a disputed event.
Free-form context-limited queries make result membership implicit and can expose more data than the audit question requires.

feedback.reason: The service can compute a complete aggregate without spending model context on every row, while IDs preserve an evidence path for drill-down.

options.text: Aggregate and filter in the service or programmatic tool, expose the summary and representative event IDs, and provide a separate bounded detail call.
Return the 100,000 events to a programmatic model tool, ask Claude to group them, and let the model choose drill-down IDs from its truncated context.
Use a statistically selected event sample to estimate actor/day counts, and give operators no deterministic way to inspect the excluded rows.
Expose a free-form database query and ask Claude to summarize whichever rows fit the context, without an explicit aggregate or scope contract.

prompt: A security audit asks for counts by actor and day across 100,000 event records, plus a few event IDs for drill-down. The model needs the aggregate, not every raw row. Which tool design is appropriate?

constraints: All five typed tools are used on every request and consume only 1% of context.
A second discovery round adds 400 ms and no rare capability needs deferral.
Server-side authorization at invocation must remain in force.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the inventory grows or rare tools make up most definitions, restore a critical eager set and governed deferred discovery.
details.errorCorrection: The definitions consume negligible context and every request needs them, so discovery adds avoidable latency and complexity.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends loading the most critical tools while deferring others for discovery when the tool inventory is large. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The inventory is small, stable, and universally needed, so eager exposure is preferable to deferred discovery.
details.scenarioApplication: Load all five governed tool definitions in the initial request, retain server-side authorization and typed schemas, and reserve discovery for a future inventory change.
details.transfer: Keep a small universal typed catalog eager when context cost is negligible and discovery adds latency; retain authorization at invocation.

messages.text: The definitions consume negligible context and every request needs them, so discovery adds avoidable latency and complexity.
This creates the measured second-round latency even though all five tools are universal and already fit comfortably in context.
Replacing typed definitions removes contract clarity and does not improve authorization; invocation enforcement must remain independent of prompt exposure.

feedback.reason: The context and latency evidence reverses the large-inventory default: eager core plus deferred tail has no tail to defer here.

options.text: Use a discovery mechanism first and defer every tool because eager capability exposure is always harmful.
Eagerly load the five governed typed tools and retain invocation authorization; defer discovery until the inventory changes.
Expose only search and fetch initially, then discover update, notify, and close for each route that needs them.
Flatten the five definitions into prose and let the model choose calls without typed schemas, using the server only for transport.

prompt:
A small internal assistant has five tools: search, fetch, update, notify, and close. All five are used by every request path, their typed definitions total 1% of context, and the server can enforce authorization at invocation.

Which tool-surface strategy is proportionate to this small, universal inventory?

constraints: Wrong-tool selection rose from 0.5% to 4.2% after twelve tools were added, while transport p95 stayed stable.
Two tools have similar names but different tenant filters.
The application can version the inventory and trace tool, parameters, authorization, and outcome.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If traces show the errors come from a single malformed backend response rather than selection, repair that contract and keep the tool surface unchanged.
details.errorCorrection: The defect is wrong selection and parameters, not transport latency; extra visibility and randomness can increase the ambiguity.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic notes that tools with similar names can lead to wrong tool selection and incorrect parameters. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The capability surface needs schema clarity and observable selection outcomes; latency alone cannot identify or repair the new tool-choice failure.
details.scenarioApplication: Split overlapping capabilities into canonical tools with distinct required filters, version the inventory, and trace the selected tool, parameters, authorization, and result before expanding the catalog.
details.transfer: When selection errors rise after a catalog change, trace inventory version, chosen operation, and parameters before repairing ambiguous contracts; healthy transport is not selection evidence.

messages.text: The defect is wrong selection and parameters, not transport latency; extra visibility and randomness can increase ambiguity.
An optional filter hides a material tenant distinction and can make an incorrect scope look valid instead of requiring the correct typed field.
Descriptions may help, but without canonical required fields, versioning, and selection traces the observed choice and parameter failure cannot be diagnosed.

feedback.reason: The decision addresses both capability bloat and the evidence needed to determine whether the repair works.

options.text: Keep all tools visible and tune model temperature because the transport p95 metric is healthy.
Merge the similar tools behind one broad tool with an optional tenant filter so the model has fewer names to choose from.
Split overlapping tools with required filters, version the inventory, and trace selection, authorization, parameters, and outcomes.
Add aliases and longer descriptions to the existing catalog, but keep only final-answer logging because selection traces add overhead.

prompt:
After a catalog release adds twelve tools, wrong-tool selection rises from 0.5% to 4.2% while transport p95 stays unchanged. Two tools have similar names but different tenant filters, and traces record only the final answer, not the selected tool or inventory version.

Which catalog repair makes tool selection observable and less ambiguous?

constraints: Supplier search, contract retrieval, and summarization are the high-use path.
Rare governed capabilities must remain available without occupying the initial context.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Discovery adds one step for rare requests, but it preserves the long tail while reducing initial context pressure and wrong-tool selection.
details.errorCorrection: Treat tool descriptions as part of the context budget and capability boundary rather than exposing every operation merely because it exists.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A curated initial inventory keeps high-use tool contracts visible while tool search or another controlled discovery mechanism loads detailed rare capabilities only when relevant.
details.scenarioApplication: The assistant can search suppliers, retrieve the selected contract, and summarize it directly; an approved discovery path handles uncommon export or mutation workflows.
details.transfer: For a large tool catalog, measure use and selection quality, keep the narrow high-use surface eager, and discover governed long-tail tools on demand.

messages.text: Loading all definitions recreates the context bloat and leaves similar or rare capabilities competing with the three required tools.
Removing capabilities turns a context problem into an unsupported manual process and loses legitimate procurement workflows.
A universal schema hides distinct contracts behind optional parameters and can increase invalid combinations and selection errors.

feedback.reason: The common workflow needs precise schemas immediately; rare capabilities can be discovered when their governed use is actually selected. This reduces context and selection ambiguity without deleting valid behavior.

options.text: Expose all twenty tools at startup so Claude can choose among every procurement capability without a discovery step.
Keep the three precise read tools available for this workflow and defer rare governed tools to an explicit discovery path.
Remove every tool except a text generator and have procurement staff perform supplier and contract lookups outside the assistant.
Expose only one universal procurement tool with optional parameters so the model sees fewer names while retaining every operation.

prompt: A procurement assistant has twenty available tools, but its current workflow only searches suppliers, retrieves one contract, and summarizes it. Tool descriptions consume much of the initial context. Which configuration is the best first release?

constraints: Tool visibility must follow the validated requesting tenant and user.
High-use authorized reads should be immediate, while rare governed capabilities remain discoverable.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Tenant-scoped discovery adds filtering and invocation checks, yet it retains rare business behavior without exposing unauthorized schemas or actions.
details.errorCorrection: Separate context optimization from authorization: defer capabilities by use, but never let a model-visible catalog grant access.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Tenant and user identity scope the catalog and discovery results, while the server rechecks current permission at invocation before executing a tool.
details.scenarioApplication: Expose the municipality's three core reads, discover regional forms and exports only for that tenant, and reject a stale or cross-tenant request at the server boundary.
details.transfer: In multi-tenant catalogs, curate the eager set by validated access and usage, then enforce the same scope again at execution.

messages.text: A global eager catalog consumes context and exposes irrelevant or unauthorized capability descriptions to every municipality.
Frequency alone is not a reason to delete valid regional behavior; discovery can preserve it without eager context cost.
Prompt wording is not an authorization boundary and can be bypassed by a manipulated or stale request.
Without an eager authorized core, the common path is either bloated with irrelevant tools or lacks its precise read contracts.
Without tenant-scoped discovery and an invocation recheck, rare tools can leak across municipalities or execute after permissions change.

feedback.reason: The common capability surface can be curated per tenant, but rare tools should remain available through controlled discovery. Discovery and execution both need tenant-aware authorization; visibility alone is insufficient.

options.text: Load all 80 definitions for every municipality so the model can discover regional differences from the catalog.
Keep the authorized high-use reads eager and defer rare regional tools so ordinary requests retain their precise contracts without the full catalog.
Delete rare regional tools from the catalog because their low frequency makes their maintenance cost disproportionate.
Show every tool to the model but rely on municipality names in the prompt to prevent cross-tenant calls.
Scope discovery results by validated tenant and user, and recheck the current operation scope at invocation before executing a discovered regional form or export.

prompt: A building-permit platform serves three municipalities through one catalog of 80 tools. Each municipality authorizes a different subset; three core reads dominate, while regional forms and exports are rare. Which TWO configuration decisions preserve capability and authorization? Select TWO.
